title: Guidance on AI detection, and why we're disabling Turnitin's AI detector
author: Vanderbilt University (Brightspace / Center for Teaching)
summary: A university's public explanation for switching off Turnitin's AI detector: at its own submission volume the false-positive rate would have wrongly flagged thousands of papers a year, and Turnitin would not explain how the score is produced.
who_for: Teachers and heads of department being pushed to adopt an AI detector and needing a credible institutional refusal - and the students most likely to be wrongly accused by one, whom the page addresses directly.
skip_if: You want current accuracy numbers - this is from August 2023 and the figures have moved since. Skip if you want an alternative to detection; it does not give you one. And never treat any detector score as proof against a student - false accusations fall hardest on non-native English writers.
notes: Nearly three years old, so treat the specifics as history - but it remains the most-cited institutional decision on AI detection, and Cornell, Pittsburgh and others followed. Account tracking - Needs Cowork with Salesforce, Intercom and Google Drive connected, plus usage exports and a success plan already on file - the health score is only as good as those three inputs.

Call prep - Needs a working folder with the actual mutual action plan, call notes and proposal for this specific account - a generic prep sheet with no account files behind it has nothing real to summarize.

Create a sales proposal presentation - Needs Google Drive connected plus Extended Thinking turned on, and your company logo uploaded for color extraction - without those the deck won't match your existing proposals or brand.

Create sales reports - Needs the HubSpot connector enabled plus a sales goals document as reference context - without the goals doc, the report has no target to measure performance against.

Log sales calls to your CRM - Claude in Chrome needs a paid plan, and it works by borrowing your existing logged-in Calendar and Salesforce browser sessions rather than any API integration - so it needs you already logged into both in Chrome.

Pipeline reviews - Needs Salesforce and Google Drive connected plus a stage exit criteria reference document - scores deals against your own defined stage criteria, so it needs those criteria to already exist and be written down.

Prepare for sales deals - Needs the HubSpot connector enabled in Settings > Capabilities - and its real value is mining unstructured call notes for patterns, so it needs your CRM to actually have detailed free-text notes, not just structured fields.

Renewal risk audit - Needs a renewal book CSV, a product-usage CSV and QBR notes already in a working folder - the red/yellow/green score is only as good as those three inputs being current.

Transcript theme extractor - Needs a working folder of transcript files, and its scheduled version specifically reports the delta against the prior quarter's themes - so a single run misses the comparison that makes it useful over time.

Prep scattered documents for a compliance audit - Needs Claude Desktop plus you supply the actual audit scope or control framework (SOC 2 in the worked example) - without a named framework to map against, there's nothing to sort the documents by.

Regulatory and compliance - The Regulatory Legal plugin needs a Team/Enterprise admin to enable the Claude for Legal source first, and the initial /cold-start-interview indexing pass can take 10+ minutes on its own before you even start.

Track discovery timelines and analyze patterns - Needs your own discovery documents uploaded (PDF/Word/Excel/email) - the worked example is a ~40-document software contract dispute, so it's built for real litigation volume, not a handful of files.
